ModelMetadata.Author: Wayroo Payments
ModelMetadata.Description:
The DynamoDB table Wayroo.Payments keeps a store's payment provider configuration in. Deployed as {environment}-PaymentConfiguration; the environment prefix comes from the CDK (see Wayroo.Payments.Infrastructure/Resources/PaymentConfigurationTable.cs), so this model carries the unprefixed name.

One partition per store, so everything about a store is a single query and never a scan. Two kinds of item share that partition, which is why this model has two facets:

  * Provider configuration, sort key = the provider id (propay, adyen). One per provider the store has. Three independent writers land on it in no fixed order, so every writer uses UpdateItem naming only the attributes it owns. A whole-item PutItem by any of them would erase another's work, taking live payment credentials or a store's recorded standing with it. That is why several sample rows here are partial: an attribute is absent until its writer has run.

  * Store routing, sort key = the reserved literal #routing. One per store. Holds which provider the store acquires through and where it sits in the provider migration. Anything listing a store's providers has to skip this sort key or it hands back a provider configuration that is not one. A store with no routing item transacts through the platform default, which is what let this ship without a data backfill.

ConfigurationVersion is incremented server-side with ADD, never written from a value read earlier, and travels as the StoreProviderConfigChanged event's Sequence.

Sample values are illustrative only. The two JSON payload attributes really hold provider credentials and account PII, so the samples here are labelled placeholders rather than realistic values.

Access patterns, the attribute-by-attribute reference and the writer-ownership rules are in Docs/README.md next to this file. Not represented here: point-in-time recovery, the DynamoDB stream and the KMS encryption setting, all of which live in the CDK.

AccessPatterns.Name: UpsertConfiguration
AccessPatterns.Description: PK (StoreId) + SK (ProviderId). The provider-webhook recorder merging the credential payload in. Owns ProviderConfiguration and nothing else.

AccessPatterns.Name: UpsertAccountDetails
AccessPatterns.Description: PK (StoreId) + SK (ProviderId). The account refresh merging the provider's account information in. Owns ProviderAccountDetails, AccountStatus and AccountDetailsRefreshedOn. Shares the item with UpsertConfiguration, which is why neither may use PutItem.

AccessPatterns.Name: GetStoreProviderConfiguration
AccessPatterns.Description: PK (StoreId) + SK (ProviderId). One provider's configuration for one store.

AccessPatterns.Name: GetAllStoreConfigurations
AccessPatterns.Description: PK (StoreId) only. Every provider configuration for a store, in one partition query. The caller must skip the #routing sort key, which is in the same partition but is not a provider configuration.

AccessPatterns.Name: GetRouting
AccessPatterns.Description: PK (StoreId) + SK (the literal #routing). Which provider the store acquires through. Absent for most stores, which then fall through to the platform default.

AccessPatterns.Name: UpsertRouting
AccessPatterns.Description: PK (StoreId) + SK (the literal #routing). A provider cutover. Writes AcquiringProviderId and MigrationState, and increments ConfigurationVersion with ADD so two concurrent writers cannot land on the same version.
